deep.reconstruction:
Context: an ideal theory of operators between Hilbert spaces E, F, built from a 'Schatten norm' N on finitely supported sequences R^(N). Modern name: a symmetric norming (gauge) function. For an operator u, N(u) is N applied to the singular values t_i(u). L^N(E,F) is the maximal ideal {u : N(u) < ∞}. L_N(E,F) is the closure of the finite-rank operators E'⊗F in it. The sequence spaces ℓ^N and ℓ_N are defined the same way. N° is the dual norming function.

The previous page set up these definitions, adjoint invariance, the ideal inequality N(vu) ≤ ||v|| N(u), Hölder-type inequalities (24)-(25) and the trace pairing.

This page:
(4) Duality. Using the trace pairing <u,v> = Tr uv, the dual of L_N(E,F) is L^{N°}(F,E). If E and F are infinite-dimensional, the following are equivalent:
 a) L_N(E,F) is reflexive;
 b) L^N(E,F) is reflexive;
 c) ℓ^N is reflexive;
 d) ℓ_N is reflexive;
 plus the condition L_N = L^N and L_{N°} = L^{N°}.

(5) Item (27) is hard to read; my reading is uncertain. It most plausibly says that the sequence of 'diagonal' coefficients of u with respect to biorthogonal (orthonormal) systems satisfies N((λ_i)) ≤ N(u). In other words, the diagonal of an operator is dominated in every symmetric norm by its singular values. Grothendieck says this follows from a convexity statement.

Proof sketch of (4) on the page:
- Choose orthonormal sequences e_i in E and f_i in F.
- The map (λ_i) ↦ Σ λ_i ē_i⊗f_i embeds ℓ^N (resp. ℓ_N) isomorphically into L^N(E,F) (resp. L_N(E,F)).
- The image is complemented: the diagonal projection has norm ≤ 1 by (5). This is why (5) is needed.
- So reflexivity of L^N, or of L_N, forces reflexivity of ℓ_N.
- Reflexivity of ℓ_N gives ℓ_N = ℓ^N and ℓ_{N°} = ℓ^{N°}.
- Hence L_N = L^N, using N ≠ N_∞. Hence the dual of L_N is L_{N°} and the bidual is L_N, i.e. reflexivity.

The problem served: a Hilbert-space model for the theory of tensor norms and operator ideals. This is a test case for Grothendieck's general theory in Produits tensoriels.
errors: The proof relies on (5) for complementation, and (5) itself is stated without proof here (it is deferred: 'Tout est démontré, sauf 4. et 5.').
The list of equivalent conditions has two items labelled d) (one is a relabelled e)). The draft is messy, but the mathematics is correct: Gohberg–Krein, Schatten.
